diagram_math_checks.evidence: The defining supplier def-clifford-algebra-of-a-quadratic-space defines Cl(V,Q)=T_k(V)/J_Q and i_Q=q_Q composed with j. Both j and q_Q are k-linear, hence i_Q:V -> Cl(V,Q) is k-linear. The theorem supplies f:V -> A as a k-linear quadratic-compatible map. The diagram is explicitly on underlying vector spaces, so no algebra structure or algebra-map status is assigned to V.

Three vertices are V (upper left), Cl(V,Q) (upper right), A (lower right). The horizontal i_Q goes V -> Cl(V,Q), diagonal f goes V -> A, and dashed vertical bar(f) goes Cl(V,Q) -> A. All three agree exactly with the Statement. There are no reverse arrows or extra identities.

The only asserted commuting relation is bar(f) composed with i_Q = f. Proof 1.1 constructs tilde(f) with tilde(f) composed with j = f; proof 2.1 uses the condition f(v)^2=Q(v)1_A to factor through q_Q; proof 3.1 substitutes i_Q=q_Q composed with j to obtain the displayed relation. The Remarks repeats the quadratic compatibility condition, and retains all inherited field and quadratic-space hypotheses.

The dashed arrow marks the unique unital k-algebra homomorphism, not uniqueness among all linear maps. Proof 3.1 shows any other unital algebra map g with g composed with i_Q=f has g composed with q_Q=tilde(f)=bar(f) composed with q_Q by the tensor universal property; surjectivity of q_Q gives g=bar(f). No injectivity, nondegeneracy or inverse is depicted.
The original rigorous proof is byte-identical and precedes the new Remarks. The final explanation explicitly states that existence and uniqueness are proved independently of the illustration.
